holidays.name: National Chocolate Mint Day
holidays.description: This day is for anyone who thinks chocolate and mint belong together. Celebrate with thin mints, mint chocolate chip ice cream, peppermint patties, or a mint-laced hot cocoa. It's a cool, creamy tribute to one of the most popular flavor pairings.
holidays.origin: It's an unofficial food observance, and nobody has traced it to a specific founder. It joins the many February days that honor chocolate treats.
holidays.funFact: Mint's cooling effect comes from menthol. It activates the same cold-sensing receptors in your mouth that respond to a chilly breeze, so mint feels cold without any change in temperature.

holidays.name: International Tug-of-War Day
holidays.description: This is a day to pick up a rope and pull. Teams dig in their heels and test their strength and teamwork against each other. It honors a sport that is simple, loud, and a little bit ridiculous.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance that celebrates the sport of tug of war. Its exact founding is unclear, but it nods to the sport's long history as a contest of strength.
holidays.funFact: Tug of war was an official Olympic event from 1900 to 1920. Teams from several countries won medals in it before it was dropped from the Games.
